findings.title: The land claim changes hands
findings.claim: Pharaoh's plan to unsettle a people from their land returns in the wider Moses material as a failed claim to rule that land: his company is drowned, while the oppressed are promised succession and inherit lands. The focus's all-together phrase closes over those with Pharaoh; wider companion-group scenes distinguish their fate from the group with Moses.
findings.mechanism: The carrier أراد names a directed intention, whose content clause specifies removal from الأرض. The focus then names causative drowning and scopes it over Pharaoh and whoever is with him, جميعًا. Connections 7:128, 7:129, and 7:137 return through the land-removal relation with divine inheritance, the enemy's destruction, and the oppressed inheriting lands; 26:65–66 contrasts Moses and all with him being saved with the drowning of the others. The supplied 70:14 fragment widens the totality comparison to everyone on earth within a saving possibility. These contacts turn the local change of medium into a wider transfer of territory and group fate.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can follow the land, the ruler, and the people attached to him as one reversal: a plan to remove a community ends with the ruler's company lost and the oppressed inheriting land. All is complete within the company the focus names.
findings.containment: The focus still says that Pharaoh intended removal from land and that he and those with him were drowned; the inheritance comes from the wider connection texts, not from a new lexical gloss for الأرض. Connection 10:99 is counter-evidence to extending this territorial coercion into a general claim about compelled belief. The 70:14 target is only a supplied phrase, and its connection note's ransom framing remains qualified; no target morphology or full-context claim is added. The collective-totality branch is lexicon-qualified, and its bodily completeness facet is not applied literally.

epistemic.reason: The focus-side territorial reversal is present in a trusted cross-run publication and a legacy-unbound walk, while the wider connections provide exact Arabic but no target morphology. The totality branch is qualified and the 70:14 phrase is excerpted, so the contextual synthesis remains bounded.

findings.title: The expulsion threat returns against its author
findings.claim: The land-removal phrase in 17:103 returns in 17:76 as the same unsettling-from-land operation aimed at the Prophet, followed there by the would-be removers' brief tenure. The focus's Pharaoh instead meets drowning; 17:77 frames the earlier reversal as an unaltered pattern, making this episode one instance of a wider same-surah return.
findings.mechanism: The carrier يَسْتَفِزَّهُم with مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ meets 17:76's supplied يَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ and its stated consequence of short tenure, then 17:77 names an unchanged prior pattern. The repeated focus verb and land relation link two different targets and outcomes; the recurrence changes the focus from an isolated Pharaoh episode into a return of the removal-and-reversal operation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the focus's destabilizing verb carry a territorial edge that recurs elsewhere in the surah: the plan to unseat another does not secure lasting tenure for its author.
findings.containment: The supplied Arabic for 17:76–77 supports a same-surah echo, but target-side morphology is not supplied. The two scenes are not asserted to be identical, and 17:76's short-tenure consequence is not substituted for Pharaoh's drowning in 17:103.

epistemic.reason: The candidate's legacy-unbound wide walk supplies the focus-side nomination; exact Arabic and connection notes give a concrete 17:76–77 return, but no target morphology or independent reader identity is supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel çekirdek, hafiflik ile yerleşik ve sakin durumda kalamama arasındaki bağdır.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 17:76 repeats يَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ and states that the removers would remain only briefly; 17:77 frames the sequence as an unchanged prior pattern.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated unsettling verb and land relation meet the focus carrier, while the short-tenure result and pattern statement make the focus's drowning a distinct instance of reversal rather than a synonym for the earlier consequence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The destabilizing operation returns across the surah as a threat whose agents do not secure lasting footing.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch's ordinary unsettled-state meaning remains available; the cross-ayah contact does not claim that يَسْتَفِزَّ itself means drowning or brief tenure.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Belirli yapılarda etki, kişiyi evinden ya da bulunduğu yerden çıkarmak ve ayrılmaya zorlamak biçiminde gerçekleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The Form X verb is joined to a source phrase naming departure from the land.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 17:76 supplies the same verb-plus-land pattern and the removers' short tenure; 17:77 supplies the pattern frame.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's territorial-removal construction meets the earlier threat and its reversal, changing the local event into a repeated same-surah relation between attempted expulsion and lost tenure.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The intended removal of the Israelites is legible within a recurring pattern in which the would-be expeller's own footing is unstable.
branch_activations.boundary: The connection establishes a textual parallel, not a universal rule that every expulsion attempt has the same outcome.
